cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has finished the house of the LORD and his own royal palace, and everything he set his heart on doing for them is DONE. That man finished his WHOLE to-do list, friend, and I've had "organize the sprinkles" on mine since the day I got here.

cards.question: One night, the LORD appears to Solomon. What's the first thing He tells him?
The LORD tells Solomon He has chosen this place for Himself as a house of ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about hard days. What if He closes the sky so there's no rain, or commands the locusts to eat up the land, or sends a plague among His people?

cards.question: If hard days like that come, the LORD says He will hear from heaven if His people do something first. What is it?

answers.text: Offer more sacrifices at the temple
Ask their king to fix it

cards.text: He spells it out: if His people who are called by His name humble themselves, pray, seek His face and turn from their wicked ways. That last one is turning AROUND, like realizing you've been driving the wrong way for an hour and actually taking the exit.

cards.question: If His people do all that, the LORD says He will hear from heaven, ___ their sin and ___ their land.

cards.text: And this brand-new temple? The LORD says from now on His eyes will be open and His ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

cards.question: The LORD tells Solomon that His eyes and His heart will be at this temple for all time.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to Solomon himself: if you walk before Me as your father David walked, doing all I've commanded and keeping My statutes and ordinances. Measuring up to your dad's WALK? Friend, I'm stuck on a gold base, I can't measure up to ANYBODY'S walk, I just HOP!

cards.question: If Solomon walks before the LORD as his father David walked, the LORD says He will establish Solomon's royal ___.

cards.text: It's the same covenant the LORD made with David when He said, 'You will never fail to have a man to rule over Israel.'
But then the LORD gives the other side. If you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I set before you, and go off to serve and worship other gods...

cards.question: The LORD warns about going off to serve other gods. If that happens, what will He do to Israel?

cards.text: And the temple He set apart for His Name? He'll banish it from His presence and make it an object of scorn and ridicule among all the peoples.

cards.question: If it comes to that, the temple will become a heap of rubble, and all who pass by it will be appalled.
Passersby ask why the LORD did this to the land and the temple. What do others answer?

answers.text: They forsook Him for other gods

cards.text: And look who they walked away from: the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt. That's a heavy word to end on, friend, and Solomon heard every bit of it.

findings.problem: Cards 2, 3, 5, 9, 14 and 16 ask the baker to discover wording or an outcome that the earlier cards give no sufficient basis to reason out. Six of the nine choice cards are therefore discoveries, so most of the stop's choices are not informed guesses.

rule.text: A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Several questions rely on antecedents from cards that are no longer visible. Card 5 says "hard days like that," card 7 says "do all that," card 16 says "If it comes to that," and card 17 says "did this" without identifying the disaster in the question.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The correct answer, that the people forsook the LORD for other gods, was already stated in card 13 and repeated in card 14's setup. Card 17 therefore asks for a cause that an earlier card has already given away.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.
